question: How much does a hoops metric move when ONLY the random seed changes?
design: 8 runs, identical train_matrix.npz and identical config (mtnn_v5_concat_b2_h160_t32_d64_mlp128_fus256, 40 epochs). Seeds 7,11,13,17,19,23,29,31. Nothing else varies, so every difference below is reproducibility, not signal.
headline: test_recall has sd 0.0942 and range 0.226 across seeds. The binomial sampling sd at n=790 test pairs would be 0.0152, so the observed spread is 6.2x what a small test set explains. This is TRAINING instability.
bimodal: 3 of 8 seeds land below 0.75 test recall (0.624, 0.662, 0.668) and 5 land above 0.80. That is two clusters, not scatter — roughly 37% of runs converge to a materially worse solution with no change to data or code.
promotion_gate_is_unsatisfiable: mtnn_report.json's promotion_gate requires test recall@10 to stay within 0.02 of baseline. The measured seed range is 0.226 — 11x that tolerance. Under a normal approximation, a rerun with NO CHANGE AT ALL misses the gate with probability 0.83. The gate reads as 'is the model still as good' and actually asks 'did you draw a lucky seed'.
what_this_means_for_feature_work: The minimum detectable effect for a 3-vs-3 seed A/B is 0.2138 on test_recall and 4.27 on CQS. Both hoops feature experiments run so far reported effects near 0.004 and 0.56 — roughly 50x and 8x below what the design could resolve. Those verdicts ('inside seed noise') were correct and nearly uninformative. purity (MDE 0.0158), archetype (0.0142) and next_r2 (0.0092) are an order of magnitude more stable and are the metrics a small A/B can actually use.

denser_checkpoint_selection_refuted.hypothesis: best_epoch is picked from validation points only and --val-every defaults to 10, so over 40 epochs the trainer chooses from 5 candidates (0,10,20,30,39). A seed peaking at epoch 25 gets epoch-20 or epoch-30 weights, which would inflate the seed spread.
denser_checkpoint_selection_refuted.test: same matrix, same config, seeds 7/11/13/23/29, only --val-every 2 vs 10

result_spread.verdict: NO REDUCTION — 0.0924 vs 0.0942 on the same 5 seeds

result_backfire.what_happened: best_epoch collapsed from 30 to 6 for 4 of 5 seeds and CQS fell from ~75 to 63-67. Denser validation lets the selector chase an early transient peak in a noisy val metric; at val_every=10 epoch 6 was never a candidate. The coarse grid was accidentally PROTECTIVE, and making selection finer made the model worse.

denser_checkpoint_selection_refuted.why_it_cannot_work: corr(val_recall, test_recall) across the 8 floor seeds is +0.336 — about 11% of variance, and at n=8 not distinguishable from zero. val (n=761) and test (n=790) are near-identical in size, so this is not a sampling-size artefact. Selecting on a metric that barely tracks the reported one cannot control the reported one at ANY cadence.
denser_checkpoint_selection_refuted.what_would: purity (MDE 0.0158), archetype (0.0142) and next_r2 (0.0092) are an order of magnitude more stable than recall. Selection and small A/Bs should use those. Note corr(cqs, test_recall) = +0.980 — CQS is essentially test recall wearing a composite's name, so it inherits the same instability and is no safer to select on.

reliability_weight_does_not_reproduce.claim_in_the_code: train_mtnn.py's --reliability-weight help text records a 4-seed sweep (7/13/21/42) at alpha=0.4: 'seed-to-seed spread drops ~30% on both CQS and recall' and 'Worth defaulting to for future retrains where avoiding a seed-42-style draw matters'.
reliability_weight_does_not_reproduce.test: Same matrix, same config, 8 INDEPENDENT seeds (7,11,13,17,19,23,29,31), only --reliability-weight 0.4 vs 0.0.
reliability_weight_does_not_reproduce.verdict: DOES NOT REPRODUCE. test_recall sd 0.0942 -> 0.0819 is a 13% reduction, not 30%, and F=1.32 at p=0.722 — indistinguishable from chance. CQS sd falls 6.5% (p=0.865). purity variance gets WORSE. No mean improves (p = 0.125 / 0.264 / 0.060).
reliability_weight_does_not_reproduce.bimodality_untouched: Seeds below 0.75 test_recall go from [11,23,29] to [11,17,23,29] — the same three bad seeds plus a fourth. The lever does not rescue the bad basin it was designed for.
reliability_weight_does_not_reproduce.why_the_original_claim_looked_real: It was estimated from 4 seeds. An F-test on variance with df 3,3 has a 5% critical value near 15, so a 4-seed sweep cannot distinguish a 30% variance change from noise at all. The number was real; the confidence in it was not available from that sample size.
reliability_weight_does_not_reproduce.consequence: Do NOT default --reliability-weight to 0.4 on this evidence. The help text's 'worth defaulting to' recommendation is not supported at 8 seeds and is left at 0.0.

partial_season_hypothesis_refuted.hypothesis: eval_split() sends 2024-25 AND the in-progress 2025-26 to test (393 and 397 pairs, 50/50). probe_seed_sensitivity.py found seed 42's collapse confined to the 2025-26 cohort, so the blended test_recall looked like a stable half averaged with a fragile one. Splitting it should expose a usable stable metric.
partial_season_hypothesis_refuted.verdict: REFUTED, AND BACKWARDS. The COMPLETE season is nearly as unstable as the partial one (sd 0.1009 vs 0.1527), and BOTH are less stable than their average (0.0942). Splitting the metric would make it worse, not better.
partial_season_hypothesis_refuted.why: corr(2024-25, 2025-26) across seeds is +0.035 — the two halves are independent noise sources, so averaging them already halves the variance. Predicted sd for independent averaging is 0.0917; observed 0.0932.
partial_season_hypothesis_refuted.bad_seeds_fail_on_different_halves: seed 11 collapses on the COMPLETE season (0.537 vs 0.771); seeds 23 and 29 collapse on the partial one (0.499 each). There is no single fragile slice — probe_seed_sensitivity.py's finding was true OF SEED 42 and does not generalise.
partial_season_hypothesis_refuted.what_this_leaves: The instability is broad rather than localised, so no reweighting or re-splitting of the existing test set fixes it. The variance is dominated by which pairs a given seed happens to get right. Two levers remain untried: more test pairs (widening the test window shrinks train/val and changes the model, so not free), and reporting a K-seed mean, which costs only compute — at sd 0.0942, K=8 gives a standard error of 0.033.

CORRECTION_paired_floor.what_was_wrong: This file and 8ddb3eb reported an MDE computed with the UNPAIRED two-sample formula (2.78 * sd * sqrt(2/n)) and used it to judge A/Bs that were PAIRED — the same seeds run in both arms. Seed effects cancel in a paired comparison, so the relevant spread is the sd of the per-seed DIFFERENCE, not the sd of either arm.
CORRECTION_paired_floor.consequence: test_recall was declared 'NOT usable at small K' with an MDE of 0.2138. The paired MDE over the same 8 seeds is 0.0196 — 6.7x tighter and perfectly usable. cqs goes from 2.6122 to 0.2998, which is BELOW the +0.5 promote bar, so that rule becomes decidable rather than hopeless. purity gains least (1.9x) because it was already stable and its seed effects were small to begin with.
CORRECTION_paired_floor.what_still_stands: The instability itself is real and unexplained — 3 of 8 seeds still land in a bad basin, and four candidate fixes are still refuted. The enforced S2 gate (test_recall >= 0.80 ABSOLUTE) is unaffected: it compares one run to a fixed threshold, not two arms to each other, so pairing does not help it and the config's 0.7582 mean is still below the bar.
CORRECTION_paired_floor.found_by: An adversarial verifier in the per-model hill-climb workflow, which flagged that the estate had been budgeting experiments against a floor 7x too pessimistic for the designs actually being run.
